items.title: Johnny DeDroit Interview, 1973-03-16
items.q: I had a big band, Fakin' in the dark... A man said to me, he said, your piano player, he's on the piano more than he's on top of it.

ctx.x: The first thing he'd do is say, why are you all drinking? You know what I mean? And Cuny didn't drink. And Cuny used to be the reason why we used to, when we played on the courthouse steps during the Spring Fiesto, I had a big band, Fakin' in the dark, you know. Oh, come the way, it's a trip. You can't forget this, you know. A man said to me, he said, your piano player, he's on the piano more than he's on top of it. I said he's repairing the pedals now, he just got through with the keys. He tuned the piano. He…

You know? He just played the wrong instrument. I did the same thing at the Gulfport Institute over there, college over there, military school. The piano was so bad that the saxophones' mouthpiece were falling. I said, shove him in. Don't play the piano. No one knew that he didn't play the piano all night. So then the portable pianist came out. And Russ Papaya bought himself one. And I was about to buy one. But I decided to quit the pianist to get my voice away. And it canceled. She was so sick. So I quit. And so…
